title: kv-cache: adaptive spillover & defrag heuristics v34 to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Arielle Tan
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and frequent paging/spillover remain a primary source of tail latency and increased GPU memory churn for long-lived streaming sessions. This PR introduces v34 of the adaptive spillover + defragmentation heuristics: a combined policy that (1) prioritizes co-located KV pages for compaction to reduce fragmentation, (2) uses a low-overhead sliding-window access frequency estimator to avoid evicting recently active prefixes, and (3) decouples spillover scheduling from eviction to allow background compaction with configurable throttle windows. Changes are gated behind runtime flags and a staged rollout to Dedicated clusters. The patchset includes unit+integration tests, a microbenchmark harness (latency/throughput under synthetic multipart sessions), and a small e2e experiment run on internal canary clusters. Reasoning: earlier heuristics caused oscillation under mixed short/long session workloads because pages were evicted and immediately re-populated. The new adaptive decay factor and coalescing pass reduce churn by ~25% in our synthetic runs while lowering median and 95th percentile paging events. Rollout plan: enable default-off in main, enable for internal dedicated canaries, collect metrics for 2 weeks, then enable cluster-by-cluster. See linked linear cards for perf goals and telemetry dashboards.

review_comments: Samir Patel: Left a few inline questions about lock ordering in compactor.cc. Can we hold a lightweight 'scan' lock while building the compaction candidate list instead of the full page lock?
Arielle Tan: replied: switched to scan lock; added asserts and a perf test to validate no contention regression.
Jessie Liu: request changes: add metrics for 'compaction_runs' and 'compaction_bytes_reclaimed' and ensure they are emitted in low-overhead mode.
Arielle Tan: updated and pushed commit to add metrics; CI green for unit tests.
Priya Nair: approved after bench numbers show ~25% reduction in paging events on mixed workloads. Recommend backport to 2.14.x if rollout goes well.
ci_checks: benchmark-ci: unstable (one flaky run, re-ran and passed)
notes_on_testing: Unit tests added for fragmentation and coalesce edge cases. Microbenchmarks run with 1000 concurrent simulated streams against a small-model runtime to measure paging events and end-to-end latency. Canary runs executed on 3 dedicated pools for 72h each and telemetry collected via new counters.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: background compaction could compete with serving threads if not throttled. Mitigation: compaction runs are rate-limited by kv.spillover.throttle_ms and a low-priority worker pool; feature flags allow rollback; added canary gating and observability before wider rollout.
release_notes: Adaptive KV cache spillover and defragmentation heuristics (v34): reduces fragmentation and paging for mixed short/long streaming workloads; opt-in via kv.defrag.enabled; includes telemetry counters and rollout guidance in ops docs.
